column_boundaries.tail_text: with national security amid rising geopolitical risk
column_boundaries.head_text: When it comes to international trade, countries have always weighed economic efficiency against national security. After World War II, they pursued free international trade through low tariffs in the belief that it was both economically efficient and politically stabilizing. World trade tripled as a share of GDP between 1950 and its peak in 2008, with about half of this trade in intermediate goods, reflect- ing the importance of cross-border pro- duction relationships. Although conflict continued, there were no global-scale wars like those that characterized the first half of the 20th century. Globaliza- tion and stability had won out.
